reviewed_contracts: Original case remains in the same parallel test binary roster; its business body executes once in the owned same-binary exact-selector child.
Original three full span-chain assertions and inner five-second snapshot timeout are unchanged.
Parent adds a stricter five-second end-to-end bound measured before spawn; this is not represented as the original whole-test budget. Both pending and completed-after-deadline paths fail.
Command-private child mode; invalid mode rejects. Child has no recursively spawned test harness mode. No global environment mutation.
OwnedChild Drop kills and waits on the direct owned process on timeout, wait error or cancellation. Normal try_wait completion is reaped before captured file reads.
TempDir output files avoid blocking child pipes. Raw stdout and stderr are forwarded after reap, before result and UTF-8 assertions; no silent failed-body success.

Standalone stderr start/end markers each require exactly one occurrence; stdout requires exactly one running-1-test marker, the original exact name, and one successful 1-passed/0-failed/0-ignored summary.
A successful parent delegation return is not a test skip or capability early return.
No print lint allow was added; new forwarding uses std::io::Write and marker writes have leading newlines.
scope_limits: The actual original Windows first-registration thread ordering was not observed.
This is a fixture isolation repair, not a tracing-core concurrency fix.
Actual compilation, Windows process startup within five seconds, full same-process parallel Core coverage and the original Windows Bazel sharded target remain pending.
The observed original body uses the loopback environment-info fixture with ShellSnapshot::disabled; no new process-tree cleanup guarantee is claimed.
